_comment: Scope-detection config for the Data Quality Gate (distinct from data-standards' .data-standards.json). Read by .claude/skills/data-quality-gate/scripts/scope_detect.py, stdlib-only, no PyYAML/psycopg needed for this step so an irrelevant PR returns NOT_APPLICABLE cheaply and fast.
_migration_command_note: dashboard/database/migrations/ is NOT self-sufficient — it's a set of incremental deltas layered on top of the base schema in infrastructure/supabase/00_complete-schema.sql (confirmed live: applying migrations/ alone to an empty throwaway Postgres fails immediately with 'relation "conversations" does not exist', since that table — and most of the core schema — is only defined in 00_complete-schema.sql, never inside migrations/ itself). 01_rls-policies.sql is deliberately SKIPPED — confirmed it references Supabase's own built-in "auth" schema (auth.uid()/auth.jwt()), which only exists inside a real hosted Supabase project and fails on any plain throwaway Postgres; it also contains zero schema-structural statements (no CREATE TABLE/ADD COLUMN/CREATE INDEX, purely 124 row-level-security policies), so skipping it has no effect on what this gate actually checks. 11 real migration files (plus the base schema) also GRANT to Supabase's managed 'authenticated'/'service_role' roles, which don't exist on a plain Postgres either — confirmed live ('role "service_role" does not exist'); migration_command creates both as empty, no-login stand-in roles first (matching how Supabase's own local-dev CLI already handles this), safe unconditionally since every CI run gets a brand-new, role-free container. dashboard/database/migrations/009_create_ama_tables.sql also fails live ('schema "auth" does not exist') — unlike 01_rls-policies.sql this file cannot be skipped, since it mixes real CREATE TABLE statements (ama_conversations, ama_messages, ama_query_audit) together with 4 auth.uid() references inside its own RLS policies (confirmed via grep — no other migration file or the base schema references the auth schema at all). Fixed by creating a stand-in auth schema with a stub uid() function that always returns NULL::uuid before applying anything — this lets the RLS policy statements succeed harmlessly (they just never match a real user in this throwaway container) while preserving all the real table-creation DDL in 009, matching the same reasoning already used for the authenticated/service_role stand-ins above.
migration_command: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c 'CREATE ROLE authenticated; CREATE ROLE service_role;' || exit 1; psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c 'CREATE SCHEMA auth; CREATE FUNCTION auth.uid() RETURNS uuid LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$ SELECT NULL::uuid $$;' || exit 1; psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f infrastructure/supabase/00_complete-schema.sql || exit 1; for f in dashboard/database/migrations/*.sql; do psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f "$f" || exit 1; done
